tagline: Up the Patuxent with the British, as far as Fort McHenry.
intro: The byway starts in Southern Maryland near Hollywood and the fishing village of Solomons, runs up the Patuxent country by St. Leonard and Benedict to Upper Marlboro, then by Bladensburg and the Baltimore-Washington Parkway to Fort McHenry on Baltimore's harbor. It follows the summer of 1814, when the British came up the Bay.

Commodore Joshua Barney's Chesapeake Flotilla, lightly armed, shallow-draft barges meant to defend the rivers, fought the Royal Navy in several inconclusive battles, and on August 22 Barney had to scuttle it himself.

moments.title: Sotterley
moments.text: The British raided this plantation above the Patuxent during the war, and more than 50 people enslaved here claimed their freedom by fleeing to them.

moments.title: Benedict
moments.text: The British army landed at this old fishing village on August 18, 1814, and marched on Washington, routing a larger American force at Bladensburg before burning the capital.

moments.title: Fort McHenry
moments.text: After the night's bombardment a 30-by-42-foot garrison flag went up early on September 14, and Francis Scott Key, watching from a truce ship, began to write.
